trigger: Written request after full performance, and tender of the reasonable charges
duty: Mortgagee (or successors/assigns) must discharge the mortgage or execute and acknowledge a certificate of discharge or release
remedy: $300 damages plus all damages occasioned by the neglect or refusal, payable to mortgagor or successors; requires written request and tender of reasonable charges
alternative_release: Title insurer may reconvey a trust deed: notice of intent by certified mail or hand delivery to beneficiary and servicer 30+ days after payoff; record reconveyance 90+ days later if no objection.

trigger: Secured creditor receives full payment and performance, with no obligation to advance further (equity line also closed)
duty: Secured creditor (holder/beneficiary or servicer; not a trustee) must submit a satisfaction of the security instrument for recording with the probate judge
remedy: $500 to mortgagors plus actual economic damages, only if after the 30 days they send a signed written request (proof of receipt) and creditor fails to record within 21 days. Good-faith defense
alternative_release: Title insurer (or its attorney-agent) as satisfaction agent, after the 30-day deadline: notice to creditor; may record affidavit of satisfaction if none recorded within 30 days of receipt.
notes: Covers 1-4 family residential loans. Other mortgages fall under § 35-10-30: $200 if not satisfied 30 days after a request.

trigger: Request by the person making satisfaction, after the mortgagee receives full satisfaction
duty: Mortgagee must acknowledge satisfaction of record, or for a deed of trust request the trustee to reconvey (trustee reconveys on beneficiary's written request)
remedy: Forfeits to the aggrieved party any sum not exceeding the amount of the mortgage money, recovered by civil action. Clock runs only from a request
alternative_release: 60+ days after the request, a Satisfaction Affidavit may be recorded by the attorney who drew the instrument, an attorney for payer or payee, or a title agent of the title company that sent payoff.

trigger: Mortgagee, trustee or person entitled to payment receives full satisfaction of the mortgage or deed of trust
duty: Person receiving satisfaction must record with the county recorder a release, satisfaction, or deed of release and reconveyance (trustee need not join)
remedy: Actual damages after 30 days. $1,000 plus actual damages if still unrecorded 30+ days after owner's written request by certified mail identifying the instrument. Individual actions only
alternative_release: Title insurer may record release/reconveyance if none within 60 days of payoff (stated debt up to $1M): certified-mail notice no earlier than 60 days after payoff and 30+ days before recording.

trigger: Satisfaction of all secured debt AND receipt from debtor of reasonable costs of procuring/recording the release
duty: Creditor/holder must record release with clerk and recorder, or for a deed of trust file the release request with the public trustee, who releases and records
remedy: Creditor liable to owner and anyone liable on the debt for actual economic loss incl. reasonable attorney fees and costs (38-35-124(3)); same to payoff-statement addressees (38-35-124.5(2)).
alternative_release: Colorado-licensed title insurer may request the public trustee release without the original note, with deemed indemnity and an officer affidavit that it caused the debt to be paid. No waiting period.
notes: For a deed of trust, the release request goes to the public trustee, who records the release. A home equity line isn't released until it is closed in writing.

trigger: Written release request sent by registered/certified mail, or received by courier or other means (incl. electronic)
duty: Mortgagee or person authorized to release must execute and deliver a release to the town clerk (or to the mortgagor if asked in writing); copy to mortgagor
remedy: $200 per week after the 60 days, up to $5,000, or the actual loss if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees, to any person aggrieved
alternative_release: Attorney, title insurer officer or institutional payor may record a release affidavit once 60+ days pass after the mortgagee got payoff, after 15 days' certified-mail notice with the draft affidavit.
notes: § 49-8(a) requires a release on satisfaction with no day count; the 60 days run from a written request sent by registered or certified mail.

trigger: Holder's receipt of full payment of the note, or its full satisfaction (statute fixes when wires and checks count)
duty: Note holder must execute, acknowledge and deliver to the payor a release in a § 42-818.02(c) form (certificate of satisfaction, affidavit, or note marked paid)
remedy: After written request and 30 more days: $50/day penalty from the 31st day after the request until delivery, plus actual and consequential damages and costs incl. reasonable attorney fees
alternative_release: An officer of the title insurer or a licensed title agent that disbursed the payoff may record the original note marked paid or canceled with its affidavit; no waiting period stated
notes: The release is delivered to the payor; the holder doesn't record it.

trigger: Satisfaction or performance of the secured debt is completed, including payment of any required satisfaction fees
duty: Legal holder of the mortgage at payoff must cause satisfaction to be entered of record (recorded satisfaction piece or attorney's § 2120 affidavit)
remedy: Damages to the payor of $10 to $500, more if special damage pleaded and proved (§ 2114); willful failure fined up to $1,000 per failure plus costs (§ 2111(e)); court rule to compel (§ 2115)
alternative_release: Delaware attorney who paid off the loan may record an affidavit and request after 60 days from payoff and at least 15 days' certified-mail notice to the creditor; recorder then marks it satisfied
notes: The attorney's affidavit form in § 2120(f) says at least four months must have passed, though § 2120(a) says 60 days.

trigger: Loan balance fully paid, or paid per the lender's estoppel letter, whichever is earlier
duty: Mortgagee or servicer must execute and acknowledge a release, send it for recording in the county records, and send the recorded release to the mortgagor/owner
remedy: Prevailing party in a civil action to enforce the release duty gets reasonable attorney fees and costs. No statutory damages amount.
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or appointed agent may record a certificate of release if none is recorded after payoff per estoppel letter; copy to servicer. No wait stated. Loans <= $500,000, not open-end.
notes: The payoff (estoppel) letter is due within 10 days of a written request (§ 701.04(1)(a)).

trigger: Written request by any party in interest, sent by certified or registered mail, after full satisfaction of the mortgage
duty: Mortgagee or record assignee must provide the mortgagor an acknowledged, recordable release (plus reassignment of any leases/rents assignment)
remedy: Circuit court action for an order releasing the mortgage (default order if no answer in 45 days); on good cause, treble damages and reasonable attorney fees and costs unless a reasonable dispute
alternative_release: After the 60 days, a title insurer or underwritten title company may execute the release itself, signed by an officer, with an affidavit of proof of payoff (e.g. canceled check)
notes: The release is due on full satisfaction with no day count; the 60 days run from a request sent by certified or registered mail.

trigger: Payment in full (revolving/future-advance mortgage: later of payoff or borrower's written request)
duty: Mortgagee, its personal representative or assignee must execute, acknowledge and record a written instrument of satisfaction referring to the mortgage
remedy: Actual damages + $500 penalty + reasonable attorney fees (§ 655.3). Safe harbor if reasonable procedures followed in good faith and failure beyond mortgagee's control (§ 655.6).
alternative_release: Iowa Title Guaranty Division certificate of release on application by lender, broker, attorney, participating abstractor or closing agent: >30 days after payment, then 30-day notice to servicer.
notes: For a revolving or future-advance mortgage, the 30 days run from the later of payoff or the borrower's written request.

trigger: Payment of the debt secured by the mortgage or trust deed (mortgagee knowing it is paid)
duty: Mortgagee, assignee of record or trustee must execute and deliver a release to the mortgagor (or authorized person) or deliver it to the recorder for recording
remedy: $200 per offense to the party aggrieved plus reasonable attorney's fees, by civil action; court orders the release. Successor not liable if it complies within 30 days of succeeding.
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or appointed agent may record a certificate of release once paid per lender's written payoff statement; no waiting period. 1-4 family, loan < $500,000; trust deeds excluded.

trigger: Holder's receipt of the mortgagor's written demand, sent by registered or certified mail, after the debt is paid
duty: Owner, holder or custodian of the mortgage must release, discharge and satisfy it of record
remedy: Forfeit up to $500 to the mortgagor plus costs and reasonable attorney fees; court may appoint a commissioner to release the lien
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or appointed agent may record a certificate of release if none recorded within 60 days after payoff per payoff statement, after 30+ days' written notice. Loans up to $1,000,000.
notes: The release is due on payoff with no day count (§ 32-28-1-1); the 15 days run from a demand sent by registered or certified mail.

trigger: Written demand for satisfaction after payoff (certified/registered mail for closing-agent release)
duty: Mortgagee or assignee must enter satisfaction of record (or cause it to be entered), paying the fee; duty arises 'forthwith' once debt paid, no future advances
remedy: $500 plus reasonable attorney fee for preparing and prosecuting the action, plus any additional damages the evidence warrants; requires demand under § 58-2309a(c).
alternative_release: Lender or designated closing agent that paid the debt relying on mortgagee's written payoff may enter satisfaction if mortgagee fails within 20 days after written demand by certified/registered mail.
notes: The statute requires satisfaction forthwith on payment; the only day count runs from a written demand.

trigger: Date of satisfaction: lienholder's receipt of certified/cashier's check, wire or other payment sufficient to pay off
duty: Holder of any lien on real property must release it in the county clerk's office where recorded; then mail owner a copy of the release within 7 days
remedy: Court-ordered release with costs + attorney fee. If written notice ignored without good cause: $100/day from 15th day after receipt; $500/day after 45th day; plus actual expenses and fees.
alternative_release: Owner or interest holder may sue in District or Circuit Court; on proof of payoff the court directs its master commissioner to execute and file the release (no title agent affidavit process).
notes: The lender must mail the owner a copy of the release within 7 days. Per-day damages need certified-mail or hand-delivered notice.

trigger: Mortgagee's receipt of full payment of the debt in accordance with its payoff statement
duty: Mortgagee must execute and deliver to mortgagor or its agent documentation acceptable to the clerk/recorder to cancel the mortgage inscription
remedy: § 9:5385(B): mortgagee and servicer/note holder liable in solido for all damages and costs, incl. reasonable attorney fees, if note or release not produced within 30 days of written demand.
alternative_release: Title insurer's authorized officer, closing notary or payor's attorney/notary may record cancellation affidavit once >60 days have passed since payment, after >=15 days' written notice to mortgagee.
notes: § 9:5385 separately gives 30 days from a written demand to produce the paid note or a release; damages run from that one.

trigger: Mortgagee, servicer or note holder's receipt of full payment and satisfaction of the mortgage
duty: Mortgagee, servicer or note holder must record a discharge and send a copy with recording info, or give a recordable discharge to the closing attorney
remedy: Greater of $2,500 or actual damages, plus reasonable attorney fees and costs; capped at actual damages if lender cures within 30 days of a written demand sent certified, in hand or overnight
alternative_release: MA attorney may record a discharge affidavit for 1-4 family property once 45+ days pass after payoff, after 45 days' certified-mail notice to the lender (notice may go with the payoff)
notes: The lender may instead give the closing attorney a recordable discharge; the attorney then has 45 days to record it (§ 55(d)).

trigger: Principal-dwelling loan paid in full with no further commitment to advance or incur secured obligations
duty: Holder must release in a reasonable time; if not recorded or given to settlement agent to record within 45 days, must give borrower recordable release + notice
remedy: Borrower who wins suit to compel release gets costs + reasonable attorney fees (§ 3-105.1(g)), not vs licensed mortgage lenders, banks, credit unions or affiliates. No statutory damages.
alternative_release: Licensed settlement agent, title insurer or Maryland lawyer who paid off the debt may record statutory release affidavit: >=60 days after payoff, certified-mail notice with draft, then >=30 more days.
alternative_citation: Md. Code, Real Prop. § 3-105.2 (similar canceled-check route: § 3-105(c)(3))
notes: § 7-106(d): on a settlement agent's written request, any lienholder must deliver an executed release within 7 days of certified funds.

trigger: Full performance of the conditions of the mortgage (open-end credit line: written request to terminate plus payoff)
duty: Mortgage owner and any servicer receiving final payment must record a release plus needed assignments; mail recorded release to mortgagor within 30 days
remedy: $200/week after day 60 (aggregate cap $5,000) or actual loss, whichever greater; owner and servicer jointly liable. $500 if release not mailed within 30 days. Costs + attorney fees.
alternative_release: Maine attorney may record discharge affidavit for owner-occupied 1-4 family home >30 days after payoff per payoff statement, after 15 days' certified-mail notice to mortgagee.
notes: The recorded release must be mailed to the mortgagor within 30 days.

trigger: Mortgage paid or otherwise satisfied
duty: Mortgagee (or its personal representative, successor or assign) must prepare a discharge, file it with the county register of deeds and pay the recording fee
remedy: $1,000 damages to mortgagor plus all actual damages; court may award double costs. Applies if mortgagee fails within 60 days after a request and tender of its reasonable charges
notes: Damages under § 565.44 run from a request and tender of charges, not from the payoff.

trigger: Written request from the payor plus payment of the full balance; statute counts 45 days from request and from payment
duty: Lender/holder must deliver a recordable satisfaction of mortgage to the party paying off, in hand or by certified mail postmarked within the deadline
remedy: Civil penalty up to $500 plus actual damages (§ 47.208 subd. 2). Under § 507.41, actual damages if not discharged within 10 days after request and tender of reasonable charges
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or agent may record a certificate of release once payoff was sent per the payoff statement and no satisfaction is recorded; no waiting period; loans of $1.5M or less
notes: § 507.41 also requires a discharge within 10 days after a request and tender of charges.

trigger: Receipt of a certified-mail demand letter (with proof of payoff in good funds) and tender of recording costs
duty: Secured party (mortgagee/beneficiary) must submit a sufficient deed of release for recording; trustee need not join (§ 443.060)
remedy: Lesser of $300 per day after day 45 or 10% of the security instrument amount, plus court costs and attorney fees; plaintiff must prove the certified-mail demand at trial
notes: If the release is rejected for recording, the lender has 60 days from notice of the rejection to resubmit it.

trigger: Request for reconveyance (trust indenture) or for a discharge certificate (mortgage) after full performance
duty: Beneficiary/servicer must request reconveyance and trustee must reconvey to grantor; for a mortgage, mortgagee must execute, acknowledge and deliver a discharge
remedy: $500 plus all actual damages; court shall award attorney fees and costs to the prevailing party (trust indentures). Mortgages: $500 plus actual damages, 90 days after request (§ 71-1-212)
alternative_release: Title insurer or producer that paid the loan sends certified-mail notice of intent to reconvey at or after payoff; if no objection within 90 days of delivery it may record a reconveyance

trigger: Secured creditor receives full payment or performance (for credit lines/future advances, also a termination notice)
duty: Secured creditor (not the trustee) must submit a satisfaction of the security instrument (deed of trust or mortgage) for recording
remedy: Actual damages to landowner (no punitive). Plus $1,000, reasonable attorney fees and costs if landowner sends demand with proof of receipt and no satisfaction within 30 days of receipt.
alternative_release: NC-licensed attorney as satisfaction agent, after the 30-day period, gives notice to creditor and may record an affidavit of satisfaction if no response within 30 days of notice.

trigger: Mortgage or other lien on real property is satisfied (or receipt of owner's written demand, if that is sooner)
duty: Owner of the mortgage or lien must execute an acknowledged certificate of discharge and cause a satisfaction of record to be entered
remedy: Liable to property owner for all damages sustained plus $100 exemplary damages. No demand precondition. Filing fee paid by owner or added to the debt.
alternative_release: Title insurance company officer or appointed agent may record a certificate of release for a mortgage of $500,000 or less paid per a payoff statement; no waiting period stated.
notes: A written demand from the owner shortens the deadline to 30 days after it is received.

trigger: Creditor receives full payment or performance AND a written request from the borrower, successor or junior holder
duty: Secured creditor (mortgagee or deed-of-trust beneficiary) must record, or cause to be recorded, the release, satisfaction or deed of reconveyance in each county
remedy: Greater of $5,000 or actual damages plus attorney fees and costs if the borrower asked; actual damages plus fees if a successor, buyer or junior holder asked. Reasonable-procedure defense.
alternative_release: Closing agent (designated title agent or NE attorney) may record a certificate of satisfaction if no release within 60 days after payoff and after its 60-day advance notice to the creditor.

trigger: Mortgage is satisfied and reasonable charges are tendered to the mortgagee
duty: Mortgagee must record the discharge in the registry of deeds and give written confirmation of it to the payor of the final payment within the same 60 days
remedy: Greater of $200 per week after the 60 days (max $2,500) or the actual loss, plus costs and reasonable attorney fees (RSA 479:8). No written demand precondition.
alternative_release: Mortgagor, successor in title or successor's lender may record a discharge affidavit once 60 days have passed since payoff per payoff statement, after 15 days' certified-mail notice to mortgagee.

trigger: Mortgage redeemed, paid and satisfied, and the mortgagee has received all fees the mortgagor must pay for cancellation
duty: Institutional mortgagee must submit the mortgage to the county recording officer for cancellation and send the mortgagor a copy of the transmittal letter
remedy: After written notice of noncompliance: $50/day fine (max $1,000) after 15 business days; greater of actual damages or $1,000 plus fees (46:18-11.3). Suit fees need 20 days' notice (11.4).
alternative_release: NJ attorney or title producer who made the payoff may record a discharge as attorney-in-fact with affidavit: notice 30 days after payoff, intent notice 30 days later, record 15 days after.
notes: Applies to institutional mortgagees; others must notify the mortgagor within 10 days and apply to cancel within 30 days of receiving the fee (§ 46:18-11.2(a)). The demand's 15 days are business days.

trigger: Beneficiary (or mortgagee) receives written notice that the secured debt has been paid, satisfied or discharged
duty: Beneficiary must deliver a request to reconvey (and note and deed of trust) to the trustee; trustee must record reconveyance within 45 calendar days
remedy: $1,000 plus reasonable attorney fees and costs to the grantor; actual damages plus fees to any party to the deed of trust; willful violation is a misdemeanor.
alternative_release: Title insurer may record a release if no reconveyance within 75 calendar days after payoff (90 if paid before 10/1/1993), after 30 days' mailed notice; blocked by contrary written instructions.
alternative_citation: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 107.077(4)-(6); § 106.290(3)-(5) for mortgages; § 107.079 surety bond route
notes: The clock runs from written notice of the payoff. The trustee must then record the reconveyance within 45 days.

trigger: Payment of principal, interest and other amounts due has actually been made (credit-line mortgages: on written request)
duty: Mortgagee must execute a satisfaction and within 30 days present it for recording (or to the mortgagor if requested); note and mortgage returned within 45 days
citation: N.Y. Real Prop. Acts. Law § 1921(1)(a); N.Y. Real Prop. Law § 275(1)
remedy: $500 if not presented within 30 days, $1,000 within 60, $1,500 within 90 (lenders making 5+ loans/yr). Owner-occupied 1-6 family: $500 or economic loss if not delivered in 90 days (1921(4)).
alternative_release: Owner-occupied 1-6 family or condo: any attorney may file a discharge affidavit if no satisfaction within 90 days of payment, after notice 30+ days post-payoff; recorded unless objection in 35 days.
notes: The note and mortgage must be returned within 45 days. For owner-occupied 1-6 family homes, § 1921(4) adds a 90-day delivery rule.

trigger: Date of satisfaction: obligation paid in full and terminated, with no further advances possible
duty: Mortgagee (original or any successor/assignee) must record a release of the mortgage in the county recorder's office and pay the recording fees
remedy: $250 civil damages, no notice needed (C). After 90 days owner may send written notice; if not recorded 15 days after delivery: $100/day up to $5,000 plus attorney fees and costs (D)-(E).
notes: $250 is owed without notice. After the 90 days, a written notice opens a further remedy if the release isn't recorded within 15 days: $100 a day up to $5,000.

trigger: Payment of the debt secured by the mortgage (or judgment lien)
duty: Holder of the mortgage must release it and file the release with the county clerk where the mortgage is recorded
remedy: After 30 days, written request; if no release within 10 days, penalty of 1% of principal, max $100/day, total capped at 100% of principal. Title insurer's attorney may sue for mortgagor.
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or agent may record an affidavit (operates as release) if no release delivered within 60 days after payoff per payoff statement, after 15 days' certified-mail notice.

trigger: Performance (payoff) of the obligation secured by the trust deed
duty: Beneficiary must deliver a written reconveyance request to the trustee; trustee must then reconvey within 30 days after receiving it
remedy: Refusing beneficiary/trustee liable as in ORS 86.140: $500 plus actual damages. 86.140 liability arises on failure to discharge within 30 days after request and tender of reasonable charges.
alternative_release: Title insurer or insurance producer may record a release of trust deed if no reconveyance recorded within 60 calendar days of payoff, after 30 days' mailed notice with no written objection.
notes: The beneficiary's 30 days are to ask the trustee to reconvey; the trustee then has 30 days after receiving the request. Mortgages run only from a request (ORS 86.140).

trigger: Mortgagee gets BOTH full payment plus satisfaction/recording costs AND the mortgagor's first written notice to satisfy
duty: Mortgagee (holder, servicer, or their agents/assigns) must present a satisfaction piece for recording in the office where the mortgage is recorded
citation: Mortgage Satisfaction Act, Act of Dec. 9, 2002, P.L. 1530, No. 197, §§ 4, 6(d) (21 P.S. §§ 721-4, 721-6)
remedy: Penalty up to the original loan amount, plus costs and reasonable attorney fees; individual actions only, no class; § 6 is the exclusive damages remedy. Notice by certified/registered mail.
alternative_release: Residential 1-4 units: 90 days after payoff with no satisfaction, a settlement officer (title agent, insurer employee, PA lawyer) may send notice of intent, then record 60 days after its receipt.
notes: Satisfaction is due on payment, but the only day count runs from payment plus the mortgagor's first written notice.

trigger: Final payment: mortgagee receives full satisfaction of the money due on the mortgage
duty: Mortgagee must discharge the mortgage (entry or separate release), send the discharge for recording, and notify the mortgagor
remedy: Penalty $50 for first day of noncompliance + $5/day after, plus reasonable attorney fees (34-26-5(b)). Separately, damages, attorney fees, triple costs if no release 10 days after request.
alternative_release: Attorney or title insurer officer may record a release affidavit once more than 60 days have passed since payoff and 30 days' certified-mail notice draws no written response.

trigger: Request by certified mail (or delivery with proof) from mortgagor or interested party, plus tender of recording fees
duty: Holder of record of the mortgage (deed of trust treated alike) must enter satisfaction in the proper recording office
remedy: Forfeit up to one-half of the secured debt or $25,000, whichever is less, plus actual damages, costs and attorney's fees in the court's discretion; court orders satisfaction entered.
alternative_release: Any SC-licensed attorney with proof of payment to the mortgagee/servicer may record a Mortgage Lien Satisfaction Affidavit; it releases the lien. No waiting period stated.

trigger: Mortgage or other lien satisfied by payment, foreclosure, or other legal means
duty: Lienholder must deliver a sworn satisfaction to the debtor (statute says deliver, not record); on owner's written demand, within 10 days of receipt
remedy: If no sworn satisfaction within 10 days of receipt of a proper written demand: all damages sustained, attorney's fees, plus a $100 penalty.
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or appointed agent may record a certificate of release (mortgages of $500,000 or less) if no satisfaction recorded after payoff per payoff statement; no waiting period stated.
notes: The sworn satisfaction is delivered to the debtor; the statute doesn't require the lienholder to record it.

trigger: Mortgage servicer or mortgagee receives the correct payoff amount for a home loan from the mortgagor
duty: Mortgage servicer or mortgagee must deliver a release of lien to the mortgagor or file it with the county clerk for recording
remedy: No damages or fees stated in § 343.108; § 343.108(d) says Chapter 349 (Finance Code penalties) does not apply.
alternative_release: Title insurer officer or authorized title agent may record an Affidavit as Release of Lien after payoff per payoff statement and notice to mortgagee; mortgagee may controvert within 45 days of notice.
notes: Home loans only. If the borrower sends a written request within 20 days after payoff, the release is due 30 days after the request is received (§ 343.108(c)).

trigger: Secured lender or servicer's receipt of the final payment of the loan
duty: Secured lender (mortgagee or trust deed beneficiary) or servicer must release the security interest within 90 days after receipt of final payment
remedy: Greater of $1,000 or treble actual damages (incl. quiet title costs) plus reasonable attorney fees and costs. Defense: reasonable release procedure followed in good faith, delay beyond its control.
alternative_release: Title insurer/agent that paid off (or has satisfactory evidence) sends notice of intent to lender/servicer; if no release recorded and no certified-mail objection in 60 days, it may record release.
notes: A trust deed's trustee must reconvey on the beneficiary's written request, with no day count (§ 57-1-33.1).

trigger: Full payment of the secured debt; or, if a settlement agent so requests, receipt of the settlement agent's notice
duty: Lien creditor (or later holder) must deliver a recordable certificate of satisfaction to the clerk with the recording fee, or to the requesting settlement agent
remedy: Creditor forfeits $500 to obligor; plus court costs and attorney fees if unpaid 10 business days after certified-mail demand. Court-ordered release with fees, actual damages (§ 55.1-344).
alternative_release: Settlement agent that paid off, or title insurer, mails notice of intent with payoff letter and draft release; if no objection or release within 90 days, files certificate of satisfaction + affidavit.
notes: If a settlement agent so requests, the clock runs from receipt of its notice.

trigger: Full performance of the conditions of the mortgage; open-end credit line: payoff plus written request to terminate
duty: Mortgagee of record (holder, and servicer receiving final payment) must execute and deliver a valid, complete discharge plus proof of its authority
remedy: Holder and servicer jointly liable: $25/day after the 30 days, max $5,000 aggregate for all aggrieved parties, plus consequential and punitive damages, costs and attorney fees (§ 464(d)).
alternative_release: Vermont-licensed attorney may record a discharge with affidavit, at mortgagor's request, once more than 30 days have passed since the mortgagee received payment per its payoff statement.
notes: The deadline is to execute and deliver the discharge, not to record it. A payoff statement is due within 5 business days of a written request (§ 464(a)).

trigger: Request or demand, after payment, by any person interested in the mortgaged property
duty: Mortgagee (or assigns) must execute and acknowledge a satisfaction; deed of trust beneficiary must ask trustee to reconvey (61.24.110(2) uses the 60 days)
remedy: Mortgagee forfeits and pays mortgagor damages (no amount set) and reasonable attorney fees; court, once satisfied of payment, orders the auditor to record its order.
alternative_release: Title insurer/agent, escrow agent or attorney who paid the demand may ask trustee to reconvey; if none 120 days after payment, records a declaration of payment; lien ends absent objection in 60 days.
notes: The request need not be in writing.

trigger: Creditor receives full payment/performance or the payoff-statement amount (credit lines: plus termination notice)
duty: Secured creditor (holder or authorized servicer; not a trustee) must submit a satisfaction for recording, with fees, to the register of deeds
remedy: Liable to landowner for $500 plus actual damages (no punitive) and reasonable attorney fees and costs. Defense: reasonable procedure followed in good faith, failure beyond its control (sub. 7).
alternative_release: Title insurer as satisfaction agent (1-4 family residential): notifies creditor at/after payoff; if no satisfaction recorded within 30 days after notice is effective, no objection, records affidavit.

trigger: The secured debt has been fully paid and satisfied
duty: Lienholder (incl. deed of trust and mortgage holders) must execute, acknowledge and furnish to the debtor, free of charge, a written release of the lien
remedy: On motion after notice, circuit court directs county clerk to execute the release, at lienholder's cost if refused without good cause, plus reasonable attorney fees and costs to prevailing party.
notes: The release is furnished to the debtor, free of charge; the statute doesn't require the lienholder to record it.

trigger: Mortgagee's receipt, by certified or registered mail, of a written request for discharge after full performance
duty: Mortgagee (original, current holder or its servicer) must execute and acknowledge a certificate or deed of discharge or release of the mortgage
remedy: Actual damages plus special damages of 0.10% of original principal per day after the 30 days until released, max $100/day. Mortgagee of record liable unless it names current holder within 60 days.
alternative_release: Title insurer/agent that paid off or has proof: no sooner than 30 days after payoff and after 34-1-132 request, sends notice of intent and draft release; records it absent objection in 30 days.
